mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the prior month signals an easing monetary policy cycle, which reduces discount rates for equity valuation and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 4.5%, it indicates a weakening labor market that signals economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE > 4.5, or the signal fails to outperform the market in 3 consecutive 12-month periods.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 0.5% month-over-month indicates a contraction in real economic activity, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decline > 0.5% and INDPRO decline > 0.5% MoM
failure_condition: The joint decline condition (HOUST and INDPRO both down >0.5% MoM) occurs in 20% of months but is followed by positive 5-day returns in > 40% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction drops below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle economic expansion, housing starts (HOUST) above the 12-month moving average signal robust consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: During late-cycle expansion periods, HOUST above 12-month MA is followed by negative 20-day returns in > 50% of instances, or the signal's predictive power vanishes in 3 consecutive 12-month windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) over the prior quarter indicates strengthening manufacturing output, which typically precedes positive equity returns; we expect positive 60-day S&P 500 returns when INDPRO rises.
failure_condition: INDPRO rising in the prior quarter is followed by negative 60-day returns in > 40% of cases, or the signal's Rank IC falls below 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 205, it signals accelerating inflation that triggers expectations of monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL > 205 is followed by positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances, or the signal fails to generate negative returns in 3 consecutive 12-month periods.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.5% and 0.25% respectively in the prior month signals aggressive monetary tightening amid strong labor market conditions, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 0.5% and FEDFUNDS rise > 0.25% MoM
failure_condition: The joint condition (PAYEMS up >0.5% and FEDFUNDS up >0.25% MoM) occurs in 15% of months but is followed by positive 5-day returns in > 45% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction drops below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: During high-unemployment recession periods, a rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals worsening economic conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In high-unemployment recession periods, UNRATE rising is followed by positive 5-day returns in > 50% of cases, or the signal's predictive power is absent for 3 consecutive 12-month periods.
